Consult Summary:
- 28-year-old female presents with a new-onset, unilateral left posterior headache of moderate-to-severe intensity, starting yesterday, with no associated neurological or systemic symptoms.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache.
- Onset: Began yesterday, mid-morning.
- Duration: Persistent since onset; present at time of consult.
- Progression: Built up gradually over a short period; remains intense.
- Location: Left side, at the back of the head.
- Severity: Rated as 8/10.
- Character: Throbbing.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not worsened or improved by position, time of day, or activity; Ibuprofen (Nurofen) taken yesterday with minimal effect.
- Associated symptoms: No nausea, vomiting, tingling, numbness, weakness, blurred vision, visual changes (no photophobia, no aura), eye pain, fever, chills, sweats, or rash.
- Appetite/hydration: Eating and drinking as normal.
- Previous episodes: No prior history of headaches.
- Function: No work missed, but finds it hard to perform normal activities or work due to headache.
- Systems review: Negative for neurological, visual, gastrointestinal, and systemic symptoms.

Past Medical History:
- No known medical conditions reported.
- No regular medications.
- Ibuprofen (Nurofen), dose/route/frequency not documented, taken once with minimal effect.
- No allergies reported.
- No asthma or gastrointestinal problems reported.

Social History:
- Lives with partner.
- Works as a designer.
- No smoking.
- No regular alcohol use.
- No recreational drug use.

Family History:
- Mother has hypertension and suffers from migraines.

Physical Examination:
- No examination or vitals documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations performed or reported.
- Patient has not had blood pressure checked recently.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute new-onset, unilateral left-sided headache in previously healthy young adult; no red flag symptoms.
  - Advise regular pain relief: Recommend alternating Paracetamol and a stronger pain reliever similar to Ibuprofen (specific agent not documented); to be taken with food and not concurrently with Ibuprofen.
  - Encourage rest and good hydration.
  - Advise to monitor for any warning signs including worsening pain, new neurological symptoms, fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, or recurrent similar episodes.
  - Instruct to seek further medical attention if not improving within 1–2 days or if symptoms worsen.
  - Prescription for stronger pain relief to be collected from pharmacy (specific agent not documented).

General plan items:
- Safety netting advice given, including criteria for urgent re-evaluation.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing: Allergies, medication reconciliation, physical examination, vital signs, blood pressure measurement, formal neurological assessment.
● Internal conflicts: None identified.
● Transcript quality: Good—information clear, no significant inaudible or unclear sections.
